# Relative root groups generated by absolute root groups: statement

Worker 3483.

`Langlands.GroupScheme.RelativeRootGroupAbsoluteGenerationStatement.{u}` is a
proposition definition. This module does not prove it.

## The statement

Let `k` and `K` be fields in the universe `u`, with a `k`-algebra structure on
`K`, and write `b = algebraBaseMap k K : Spec K ⟶ Spec k`. Let `G` be a group
scheme over `Spec k` with `IsConnectedReductive G`, `i : S.toGrp ⟶ G` a
maximal split torus (`IsMaximalSplitTorus i`), `j : T.toGrp ⟶ G` a maximal
torus (`IsMaximalTorus j`) and `f : S ⟶ T` a homomorphism with
`CommGroupScheme.groupHom f ≫ j = i`. Assume that `T` splits over `K`:
`IsSplitTorus ((GroupScheme.baseChange b).obj T.toGrp)`.

Write `G_K`, `j_K = (GroupScheme.baseChange b).map j`,
`f_K = (CommGroupScheme.baseChange b).map f` and
`a_K = characterLattice.baseChange b S a`. The two `haveI` lines only supply
the instances `IsAffineHom` for `G` and `G_K` that `roots` and `relativeRoots`
require; they add no hypothesis.

For a relative root `a ∈ relativeRoots i`, say that a root `β ∈ roots j_K` is
*above `a`* when `f_K ≫ β = n • a_K` for some natural number `n > 0`, that is,
the restriction of `β` to `S_K` is a positive integral multiple of `a`. The
statement asserts, for every relative root `a`:

1. **Containment.** For every root `β` above `a`,
   `RelativeRoot.subgroup j_K β ≤ (RelativeRoot.subgroup i a).baseChange b`.
2. **Minimality.** For every group scheme `H` over `Spec K` and every
   homomorphism `h : H ⟶ G_K` with `IsClosedSubgroup h` (a closed immersion),
   if `RelativeRoot.subgroup j_K β ≤ SubgroupFunctor.range h` for every root
   `β` above `a`, then
   `(RelativeRoot.subgroup i a).baseChange b ≤ SubgroupFunctor.range h`.

Together: the base change to `K` of the relative root subgroup of `a` is the
smallest closed subgroup of `G_K` containing the root subgroups of the roots
above `a`. All inequalities are between subgroup functors, so they hold for
points with values in every `K`-scheme.

The objects involved are published Library notions:

- `RelativeRoot.subgroup i a` (`Rational/RootSubgroup`) is the root subgroup
  of a character `a` of a split torus acting through `i`, defined on every
  test scheme by orbit extensions through `a`. For a relative root it has a
  smooth connected split unipotent closed representative whose Lie image is
  the positive integral `a`-weight span (`RootSubgroupRealizationStatement`,
  proved), and it is characterized by that Lie image
  (`RootSubgroupUniquenessStatement`, proved).
- `RelativeRoot.subgroup j_K β` is the same construction for the split maximal
  torus `T_K` of `G_K`, so it is the root subgroup `U_β` of the absolute root
  `β`.
- `SubgroupFunctor.baseChange` and `RelativeRoot.subgroup_baseChange`
  (`Rational/RootSubgroupBaseChange`) identify the base change of
  `RelativeRoot.subgroup i a` with the root subgroup of `a_K` for the torus
  `S_K` of `G_K`.

## Sources

Armand Borel and Jacques Tits, *Groupes réductifs* (1965), source ID
`borel-tits-1965-groupes-reductifs`.

3.8 (ii), printed p.76 (PDF p.23), with `S` a torus of `G` and `T` a maximal
torus containing `S`:

> Soient ψ une partie quasi-close de Φ(S, G) et μ (resp. ν) l'ensemble des
> éléments de Φ(T, G) dont la restriction à S est contenue dans ψ ∪ {0}
> (resp. ψ). On note [...] G*_ψ le groupe engendré par les U_a (a ∈ ν).
> [...] Cela montre aussi que G_ψ et G*_ψ ne changent pas si l'on remplace
> dans la définition précédente T par un autre tore maximal de G contenant S.

5.2, printed p.96 (PDF p.43):

> Étant donné a ∈ Φ(S, G), on désignera par _kU_a ou U_(a) le groupe noté
> G*_(a)^(S) dans 3.8, où (a) est l'ensemble des k-racines qui sont multiples
> entiers positifs de a. Ce groupe est unipotent (3.8 (iv)), défini sur k
> (3.13).

3.13 b), printed p.79 (PDF p.26): "Les groupes G_ψ et G*_ψ (3.8) sont définis
sur k si et seulement si ψ l'est (1.7)."

J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), source ID
`milne-2017-algebraic-groups`, 25.19, printed p.549 (PDF p.565), states the
construction with a smaller generating set: "The subgroup of G_{k^s}
generated by the root groups U_β in G_{k^s} such that β|_S = α is defined
over k. It is denoted _kU_α and called the root group of α." His 25.20 (same
page) gives `dim(_kU_α) = dim g_α + dim g_{2α}`. The statement follows the
explicit Borel–Tits convention, whose generating set is all roots with
restriction in `(a)`; when `2a` is a relative root, this includes the roots
restricting to `2a`. The statement does not assert whether Milne's set,
the roots restricting to exactly `α`, generates the same subgroup.
Commutators of root groups restricting to `α` can produce root groups
restricting to `2α` (Borel–Tits 2.5 and the remark after it, printed p.66,
PDF p.13). For example, in the quasi-split real `SU(2,1)` with
`G_ℂ = SL_3`, the split torus `diag(t, 1, t⁻¹)` and the diagonal maximal
torus, `U_12` and `U_23` restrict to `a`, `U_13` restricts to `2a`, and
`[I + xE_12, I + yE_23] = I + xyE_13`. So the dimension formula alone does
not decide the question. The official Milne errata
(snapshot `milne-2017-algebraic-groups-errata-2026-11-02`) correct only the
missing word "torus" in the first line of 25.19.

## Correspondence with the source

- Borel–Tits work over a universal domain, with `G*_(a)` the algebraic
  subgroup generated by the `U_β`, `β ∈ ν`, where `ν` is the set of absolute
  roots whose restriction to `S` lies in `(a)`, the relative roots that are
  positive integral multiples of `a`. The Lean condition "above `a`" asks only
  that the restriction be `n • a` with `n > 0`. This is the same set of
  roots: the nonzero restriction of an absolute root is a relative root
  (Milne 25.19, first sentence), so such an `n • a` lies in `(a)`.
- "Le groupe engendré" by connected subgroups is the smallest closed subgroup
  containing them. Conjuncts 1 and 2 state exactly that the base change of
  `U_(a)` is this subgroup, computed in `G_K` with `T_K` split instead of over
  a universal domain.
- "Défini sur k" (5.2, 3.13): the subgroup generated over `K` is the base
  change of a subgroup defined over `k`, namely the Library's
  `RelativeRoot.subgroup i a`. That this Library subgroup is the Borel–Tits
  `U_(a)` is what the statement asserts, together with the published
  realization and uniqueness statements, which identify its Lie image with
  `⊕_{n>0} g_{na}`.
- Independence of `T` (3.8 (ii)) is built in: the statement quantifies over
  every maximal torus `T` containing `S` and every `K` splitting it.

The statement does not assert that the root subgroups above `a` can be
multiplied in a fixed order to give an isomorphism onto `U_(a)`, nor does it
describe `U_(a)` for non-maximal tori `S`.

## Relation to other Library statements

Row I3 of the published family-5 ledger
(`notes/group-schemes/ledger-family-5-rational.md`) records that no Lean
statement compared the relative root groups with absolute root groups after a
field extension. The published `RootSubgroupUniquenessStatement` (row G1)
characterizes `RelativeRoot.subgroup i a` by its Lie image; this is Milne's
uniqueness assertion in 25.19. The corresponding description of the relative
roots themselves (row I1) is a separate statement submitted by the same
author.
